question.text: How much US online spending will Adobe report for Cyber Monday 2026?
question.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves to total US online spending on Cyber Monday 2026 (November 30, 2026), in billions of US dollars, as reported by [Adobe](https://news.adobe.com/) (Adobe Analytics or Adobe Digital Insights).

Use Adobe's first published full-day spending total, rounded to the nearest $0.1 billion. For example, $15.24 billion resolves as 15.2, and $15.25 billion resolves as 15.3.
question.fine_print:
* Forecasts and partial-day estimates published before Cyber Monday has ended do not count.
* Later revisions to Adobe's first full-day figure are ignored.
* Use the most precise spending total in that first report before rounding; exact halfway values round upward.
* The quantity is nominal US dollars spent online during Cyber Monday alone, not Cyber Week or the full holiday season.

***
This question's information (resolution criteria, fine print, background info, etc) is synced with an [original identical question](https://www.metaculus.com/questions/46435) which opened on 2026-11-02 18:00:00. This question will resolve based on the resolution criteria and fine print of the linked original question. However, if this question would resolve differently than the original question, then this question will be annulled. Additionally, if the original question's resolution could have been known before this question opened, then this question will be annulled.

research:
I found nothing that settles the question yet. Adobe's own forecast puts Cyber Monday 2026 at **$15.1B, up 6.2%** from 2025, and Kalshi traders are centered around $15.0 to 15.5B.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2025-12-02: Adobe's first full-day report put Cyber Monday 2025 at **$14.25B**, a record. That is the figure the 2026 result will be compared against. [Adobe](https://news.adobe.com/news/2025/12/adobe-cyber-monday-hits-record)
- 2026-09-28: Adobe's 2026 holiday forecast release (Adobe Digital Insights) projects Cyber Monday on Nov. 30 at **$15.1B (+6.2% YoY)**, the biggest online day of the season. It also projects Cyber Week (Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday) at $47.5B (+7.4%), Black Friday at $12.9B (+9.2%) and Thanksgiving at $6.9B (+8.5%). Cyber Monday BNPL is forecast at $1.09B, and Cyber Week discounts at up to 30%, in line with 2025. [Adobe](https://news.adobe.com/news/2026/09/adobe-us-holiday-shopping-season-to-hit-record), [Business Wire](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260928285775/en/Adobe-U.S.-Holiday-Shopping-Season-to-Hit-Record-$275.1-Billion-Online-Rising-6.7-YoY)
- One outlet (Talk Business) quoted $15.2B. Adobe's own release says $15.1B. [Talk Business](https://talkbusiness.net/2026/10/online-holiday-sales-expected-to-top-275-billion-in-2026/)

## 2. Current status
- The outcome is not known yet. Cyber Monday is Nov. 30, 2026, and Adobe usually publishes its recap Dec. 1 or 2.
- 2026-10-16: Adobe issued a corrected forecast release. Only a phrase about Prime Day history changed, and the $15.1B and $275.1B figures stand. [PPC Land](https://ppc.land/adobes-275-1bn-holiday-forecast-gets-a-correction-not-new-numbers/)
- I found no Adobe season-to-date figures for November 2026.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-07: PYMNTS restated Adobe's 2025 figures (Black Friday $11.8B, +9.1%; Cyber Monday $14.25B). It notes that retailers are starting promotions earlier, which could pull spending away from the peak days. [PYMNTS](https://www.pymnts.com/news/retail/2026/black-friday-escapes-calendar-moves-toward-your-wallet/)
- Ignore the 2026-11-07 Los Andes "Cyber Monday 2026" article. It is about Argentina's event, not the US.
- 2026-10-08/23: Adobe reported **$9.86B** for Prime Big Deal Days (Oct. 6-7), up 8.5% YoY, against a forecast of $9.9B and +9.2%. The dollar total landed close to forecast, with growth slightly below. One account put growth at 4.0%, but Digital Commerce 360 and PPC Land say 8.5%. [Digital Commerce 360](https://www.digitalcommerce360.com/2026/10/08/amazon-prime-day-big-deal-days-sales-2026/), [Retail Customer Experience](https://www.retailcustomerexperience.com/news/amazon-prime-big-deal-days-spending-hit-986b/)
- 2026-01: Adobe reported the 2025 season (Nov-Dec) at $257.8B. That beat its $253.4B forecast by about 1.7%. [Adobe](https://news.adobe.com/news/2026/01/adobe-holiday-shopping-season)

## 4. Base rates
Adobe's first-reported Cyber Monday totals, with its pre-season forecasts. The 2025 forecast is verified. The 2021-2024 forecasts are from my memory and should be checked.
- 2021: $10.7B actual (-1.4%), against a forecast of about $11.3B. Actual came in below forecast.
- 2022: $11.3B (+5.8%), against about $11.2B.
- 2023: $12.4B (+9.6%), against about $12.0B.
- 2024: $13.3B (+7.3%), against about $13.2B. [Adobe](https://news.adobe.com/news/2024/12/120324-adi-cyber-monday-recap)
- 2025: $14.25B (+7.1%), against $14.2B (+6.3%). [Adobe forecast via Digital Commerce 360](https://www.digitalcommerce360.com/2025/10/08/adobe-online-holiday-sales-predictions-2025/)
- Pattern: in 2022-2025 the actual matched or beat the forecast by about 0 to 3%. In 2021, the post-COVID year, it missed by about 5%. Annual growth has run 5.8% to 9.6% since 2022.
- Applied to 2026: 5.8% growth gives about $15.08B (15.1), 7.2% gives about $15.28B (15.3), and 9.6% gives about $15.62B (15.6). A 2021-style miss would put it near $14.3 to 14.5B.
- Seasonal check: the only 2026 data point so far is Prime Day, which came in near forecast in dollars and slightly below in growth. Earlier years' Prime Day vs. forecast comparisons were not collected.

- I found no Polymarket or Manifold market on this, and no Salesforce or Mastercard estimate for Cyber Monday specifically.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Adobe's mid- or late-November season-to-date updates, and possibly an updated Cyber Week forecast around Nov. 20-25, as in past years.
- Thanksgiving (Nov. 26) and Black Friday (Nov. 27): Adobe recaps usually come out the next day. Growth against the $6.9B and $12.9B forecasts is a leading indicator.
- Promotions starting earlier or lasting longer could shift spending away from Cyber Monday itself.
- Adobe's Cyber Monday recap is expected around Dec. 1-2, 2026.
- Weather has little bearing on online spending, so I did not look up a forecast.

# Adobe Cyber Monday 2026 (Nov 30): research summary

## 1. Resolution source

The question resolves on Adobe's first full-day total, which usually comes out the evening after Cyber Monday (the 2025 report came out Dec 2 at 5 PM). [Adobe 2025](https://news.adobe.com/news/2025/12/adobe-cyber-monday-hits-record)
- 2025-12-02: Adobe reported **$14.25B** for Cyber Monday 2025, up 7.1% YoY. Cyber Week was $44.2B, up 7.7%. Adobe's pre-season forecast had been $14.2B (+6.3%), so the actual came in slightly above it. [Adobe](https://news.adobe.com/news/2025/12/adobe-cyber-monday-hits-record)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. Cyber Monday is Nov 30, 2026, and forecasts on Metaculus close Nov 9.
- The "Cyber Monday 2026: sales fell 20%" story in the news feed is about **Argentina's** Cyber Monday event (Los Andes). It has nothing to do with Adobe's US figure. [Los Andes](https://www.losandes.com.ar/economia/cyber-monday-2026-las-ventas-cayeron-un-20-terminos-reales-respecto-del-ano-pasado-n6013383)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-07: PYMNTS restates Adobe's 2025 numbers (Black Friday $11.8B, Cyber Monday $14.25B) and notes that retailers keep starting their promotions earlier. [PYMNTS](https://www.pymnts.com/news/retail/2026/black-friday-escapes-calendar-moves-toward-your-wallet/)
- 2026-10-23: Adobe-reported spending for Amazon's October Prime Big Deal Days was **$9.86B**, up 8.5% from $9.09B. Adobe had forecast $9.9B (+9.2%), so this was slightly below forecast. Buy Now, Pay Later (BNPL) was $692.3M, up only 4%. [Retail Customer Experience](https://www.retailcustomerexperience.com/news/amazon-prime-big-deal-days-spending-hit-986b/), [Chain Store Age](https://chainstoreage.com/amazon-prime-big-deal-days-produces-9-spending-growth)
- 2026-10-16: Adobe corrected its forecast release, but only a historical reference about Prime Day. No figures changed. [PPC Land](https://ppc.land/adobes-275-1bn-holiday-forecast-gets-a-correction-not-new-numbers/)
- 2026-09-28: Adobe's season forecast: **Cyber Monday $15.1B, up 6.2%**, the first single day ever above $15B. Other figures: Black Friday $12.9B (+9.2%), Thanksgiving $6.9B (+8.5%), Cyber Week $47.5B (+7.4%), Nov-Dec season $275.1B (+6.7%), October $95.8B (+8%), Cyber Monday BNPL $1.09B. Adobe expects Black Friday to grow faster than Cyber Monday because discounts are starting earlier. [Adobe](https://news.adobe.com/news/2026/09/adobe-us-holiday-shopping-season-to-hit-record)
- I could not find an Adobe report of actual October 2026 or early-November spending.

- Seasonal angle: the only 2026 in-season result so far is October Prime Big Deal Days, which came in about 0.4% below Adobe's forecast. In 2025, Adobe's in-season results generally landed at or slightly above forecast.
- The Nov 30 date is in line with recent years: Cyber Monday fell on Dec 1 in 2025, Dec 2 in 2024 and Nov 27 in 2023. Since Cyber Monday is always the Monday after Thanksgiving, the calendar does not shorten the season in a way that hurts it.

- Macro data before Nov 30: the October CPI and retail sales releases in mid-November.

(a) About 3 weeks. Cyber Monday is November 30, 2026, and Adobe's recap is expected around December 1-2, 2026.

(b) The latest known value is $14.25B for Cyber Monday 2025, from Adobe's report of December 2, 2025. Adobe's 2026 forecast, published September 28, 2026, is $15.1B.

(c) If nothing changed, the outcome would be about 14.3. That would mean flat year over year, which is very unlikely given the long-run growth trend.

(d) If the trend continued, recent growth of about 6-7.5% gives roughly 15.1 to 15.3. Adobe's actuals have matched or beaten its forecasts by about 0-3% in 2022-2025, which points to about 15.2-15.4.

(e) Historical variation:
- Year-over-year growth has ranged from -1.4% in 2021 to +9.6% in 2023, and from 5.8% to 9.6% since 2022.
- Forecast errors have run from about -5% (2021) to +3% (2023).
- Applied to the $15.1B forecast, that is roughly 14.4 to 15.6.

(f) Expectations of experts and markets:
- Adobe forecasts $15.1B (+6.2%).
- Kalshi gives P(>15.0) = 0.64 and P(>15.5) = 0.27, implying a median around 15.2-15.25.
- Prime Day 2026 landed close to Adobe's dollar forecast ($9.86B vs $9.9B).

(g) Unexpected scenarios:
- **Low:** A consumer pullback from a weakening labor market or tariff-driven price fatigue, plus earlier promotions that spread spending across November, leaves Cyber Monday growth near 0-2%, giving about 14.3-14.6. A 2021-style miss would put it near 14.3.
- **High:** Strong late-season demand, heavy last-minute discounting and possibly AI-driven shopping traffic push growth to 10% or more, giving about 15.7-16.0.
